prompt: Why does a convex function have no bad local minima?
answer: If x were a local minimum and some y had f(y) < f(x), then along the segment from x to y convexity gives f(x + t(y - x)) <= (1 - t) f(x) + t f(y) < f(x) for every small t > 0, so points arbitrarily close to x would be lower, contradicting local minimality. For differentiable convex f, the tangent-plane inequality f(y) >= f(x) + grad f(x)^T (y - x) says the same: a zero gradient means no point is lower.
